items.title: ASKING A FAVOR
items.quote: When I call out, answer me, my G-d of benevolence. You relieved me in distress. Be kind to me and hear my tefillah.
items.text: If you want to ask a favor from someone, don’t start right in with your request. First, address the person courteously and make sure he is ready to give you his attention. Let him know you will appreciate anything he will do for you. This is especially important when the individual is someone to whom you owe respect.

items.title: MAKING A REQUEST
items.quote: You relieved me in distress. Be kind to me.
items.text: When you ask Hashem for something, first express your gratitude for His past kindnesses. Don’t frame your request as something you deserve or that He owes you. Rather ask Him to do it as an act of pure kindness and graciousness

items.title: ADMONISHING
items.text: When admonishing or rebuking someone, speak to him with respect, indicating that what he is doing is unworthy of him.

items.title: MAINTAINING SILENCE
items.quote: [How long] will you love empty talk, seeking falsehood?
items.text: Avoid empty talk, treachery, and falsehood. Be silent when you are tempted to utter sinful talk.

items.title: CHASIDUS
items.quote: Hashem has set apart a devout person to be His.
items.text: Develop an attitude of chasidus (being devout), that is, going beyond what is strictly required. Only then can you expect Hashem to be forgiving in His attitude towards you.

items.title: TREMBLING
items.text: Develop an attitude in which you tremble in fear of behaving badly and angering Hashem.

items.title: INTROSPECTION
items.quote: Consider in your hearts, lying in bed.
items.text: Before falling asleep at night, make an effort to think through your actions of the day to see if you have behaved badly.

items.title: SINCERITY
items.text: When correcting your behavior, think of it as a sacrificial offering that you are making to Hashem. Be sincere about your devotion and your motives.

items.title: ENVY
items.quote: Many say, ‘Who will show us the good?
items.text: Don’t be envious of the good fortune of others. Hashem gives you what is appropriate for you and that may be different from the person you are envying.

items.title: GOOD WILL
items.quote: You have put gladness in my heart from the time their grain and wine abound.
items.text: Be happy for the good fortune of another. Your positive attitude is an expression of your love for the other person.

items.title: RESENTMENT
items.quote: At peace, I will simultaneously lie down and fall asleep.
items.text: Don’t harbor resentment towards someone who has harmed you. Look to his doing teshuvah and being forgiven. Your goal should be a unity in peace.
